properties.source_locator: V1.5 Safe Deserialization, row 1.5.3 (0x10-V1-Encoding-and-Sanitization.md; PDF p.29)
properties.text: Ensure parsers for the same data format apply consistent parsing and character-encoding rules so discrepancies cannot be exploited for remote file inclusion or server-side request forgery.

properties.source_locator: V2 Validation and Business Logic › V2.2 Input Validation (0x11-V2-Validation-and-Business-Logic.md)
properties.text: Avoid DTD validation and disable framework DTD evaluation so XML external entity processing cannot be triggered through DTDs.

properties.source_locator: V5.1 File Handling Documentation, row 5.1.1 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.42)
properties.text: Document each upload feature's allowed file types, extensions, and packed and unpacked size limits, together with how unsafe downloads are prevented.

properties.source_locator: V5.2 File Upload and Content, row 5.2.1 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.43)
properties.text: Accept only files whose size the application can process without unacceptable performance loss or denial of service.

nodes.label: V5.2.2 — Validate file extension and content

properties.source_locator: V5.2 File Upload and Content, row 5.2.2 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.43)
properties.text: For accepted files and archives, verify both that the extension is allowed and that the content actually matches the claimed type.

properties.source_locator: V5.2 File Upload and Content, row 5.2.3 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.43)
properties.text: Before decompressing an archive, enforce limits on its expanded size and contained-file count.

properties.source_locator: V5.2 File Upload and Content, row 5.2.4 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.43)
properties.text: Limit both storage volume and file count per user so one account cannot exhaust storage with numerous or oversized files.

properties.source_locator: V5.2 File Upload and Content, row 5.2.5 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.43)
properties.text: Reject uploaded archives that contain symbolic links unless the feature requires them and an explicit target allowlist constrains them.

nodes.label: V5.3.1 — Prevent uploaded files from executing

properties.source_locator: V5.3 File Storage, row 5.3.1 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.44)
properties.text: Ensure files created from untrusted input and stored in a publicly reachable location cannot execute as server-side code when requested.

nodes.label: V5.3.2 — Construct file paths from trusted values

properties.source_locator: V5.3 File Storage, row 5.3.2 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.44)
properties.text: Build file-operation paths from internal or trusted values, or strictly validate any required user-supplied names or metadata to prevent traversal, file inclusion, and server-side request forgery.

properties.source_locator: V5.3 File Storage, row 5.3.3 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.44)
properties.text: During server-side file processing such as decompression, disregard user-controlled path components so extracted content cannot escape its intended location.

properties.source_locator: V5.4 File Download, row 5.4.1 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.44)
properties.text: Ignore or validate user-controlled download names and set a safe filename in the response content-disposition metadata.

properties.source_locator: V5.4 File Download, row 5.4.2 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.44)
properties.text: Encode or sanitize filenames used in response metadata or attachments so they cannot alter the surrounding message structure.

nodes.label: V5.4.3 — Scan untrusted files for malware

properties.source_locator: V5.4 File Download, row 5.4.3 (0x14-V5-File-Handling.md; PDF p.44)
properties.text: Scan files obtained from untrusted sources before serving them so known malicious content is not redistributed.

properties.source_locator: V6.1 Authentication Documentation, row 6.1.1 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.45)
properties.text: Document how rate limits, automation defenses, and adaptive responses resist credential stuffing and password guessing without enabling malicious account lockout.

properties.source_locator: V6.1 Authentication Documentation, row 6.1.3 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.46)
properties.text: Document every authentication pathway together with the security controls and authentication strength that must be enforced consistently across those pathways.

properties.source_locator: V6.2 Password Security, row 6.2.1 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.46)
properties.text: Require user-chosen passwords to contain at least eight characters and recommend a minimum length of fifteen characters.

properties.source_locator: V6.2 Password Security, row 6.2.2 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.46)
properties.text: Provide users with a way to change their password.

properties.source_locator: V6.2 Password Security, row 6.2.3 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.46)
properties.text: Require both the current password and the replacement password when a user changes a password.

properties.source_locator: V6.2 Password Security, row 6.2.4 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.46)
properties.text: When a password is created or changed, reject values found among at least the 3,000 most common passwords that satisfy the application's length policy.

nodes.label: V6.2.5 — Do not impose composition rules

properties.source_locator: V6.2 Password Security, row 6.2.5 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.46)
properties.text: Permit passwords using any character composition without requiring particular counts of uppercase, lowercase, numeric, or special characters.

properties.source_locator: V6.2 Password Security, row 6.2.6 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.46)
properties.text: Mask password-entry fields while allowing an optional temporary reveal of the full value or most recently entered character.

nodes.label: V6.2.7 — Permit password managers and paste

properties.source_locator: V6.2 Password Security, row 6.2.7 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.46)
properties.text: Allow password pasting, browser password assistance, and external password managers.

properties.source_locator: V6.2 Password Security, row 6.2.8 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.47)
properties.text: Verify passwords exactly as submitted rather than changing them through truncation, case conversion, or another transformation.

properties.source_locator: V6.3 General Authentication Security, row 6.3.1 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.47)
properties.text: Implement the documented defenses against credential stuffing and password brute force.

properties.source_locator: V6.3 General Authentication Security, row 6.3.2 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.47)
properties.text: Remove or disable default application accounts such as administrative or root accounts.

nodes.label: V6.3.4 — Enforce controls across authentication pathways

properties.source_locator: V6.3 General Authentication Security, row 6.3.4 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.48)
properties.text: Ensure every authentication pathway is documented and consistently applies the required security controls and authentication strength.

properties.source_locator: V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery, row 6.4.1 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.49)
properties.text: Generate initial passwords and activation codes with secure randomness, make them conform to the password policy, and expire them quickly or after first use.

nodes.label: V6.4.2 — Exclude password hints and secret questions

properties.source_locator: V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery, row 6.4.2 (0x15-V6-Authentication.md; PDF p.49)
properties.text: Do not provide password hints or knowledge-based authentication questions.

properties.source_locator: V13.2 Backend Communication Configuration, row 13.2.4 (0x22-V13-Configuration.md; PDF p.80)
properties.text: Constrain the external resources and systems available for outbound requests, data loading, and file access with an allowlist enforced at one or more suitable layers.

properties.source_locator: V13.2 Backend Communication Configuration, row 13.2.5 (0x22-V13-Configuration.md; PDF p.80)
properties.text: Configure the web or application server with an allowlist of the resources and systems from which it may request or load data and files.

nodes.label: V15.3.2 — Do not follow unneeded outbound redirects

properties.source_locator: V15.3 Defensive Coding, row 15.3.2 (0x24-V15-Secure-Coding-and-Architecture.md; PDF p.88)
properties.text: When the backend calls external URLs, prevent it from following redirects unless redirect handling is an intended feature.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (1)
properties.text: Design, develop, and produce the product so its cybersecurity level is appropriate to the risks identified for it.

nodes.label: AnnexI-PartI(2)(a) — Release without known exploitable vulnerabilities

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(a)
properties.text: Where the risk assessment makes this applicable, place the product on the market without known exploitable vulnerabilities.

nodes.label: AnnexI-PartI(2)(b) — Ship securely configured by default

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(b)
properties.text: Where applicable, supply a secure default configuration and a way to restore the product to its original state, subject to the stated tailor-made business-product exception.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(c)
properties.text: Where applicable, support vulnerability correction through timely security updates, default-enabled automatic installation with a clear opt-out, update notices, and temporary postponement.

nodes.label: AnnexI-PartI(2)(d) — Control and report unauthorized access

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(d)
properties.text: Where applicable, use authentication, identity, access-management, or comparable controls to prevent unauthorized access and report possible unauthorized access.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(e)
properties.text: Where applicable, protect the confidentiality of data at rest, in transit, and during other processing through current encryption or other technical safeguards.

nodes.label: AnnexI-PartI(2)(f) — Protect data and software integrity

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(f)
properties.text: Where applicable, protect data, commands, software, and configuration from unauthorized manipulation and report detected corruption.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(g)
properties.text: Where applicable, process only the data that is relevant and necessary for the product's intended purpose.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(h)
properties.text: Where applicable, preserve essential and basic functions during and after incidents, including by resisting and mitigating denial-of-service attacks.

nodes.label: AnnexI-PartI(2)(i) — Limit harm to connected services

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(i)
properties.text: Where applicable, reduce the product's and connected devices' adverse effect on the availability of other devices' or networks' services.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(j)
properties.text: Where applicable, design, develop, and produce the product to minimize its attack surface, including exposed interfaces.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(k)
properties.text: Where applicable, incorporate mechanisms and techniques that reduce the consequences of successful exploitation or another incident.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(l)
properties.text: Where applicable, record and monitor relevant internal access and changes to data, services, and functions while providing a user opt-out.

nodes.label: AnnexI-PartI(2)(m) — Support secure deletion and transfer

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part I, point (2)(m)
properties.text: Where applicable, let users permanently remove data and settings easily and securely, and protect data when it is transferred to another product or system.

nodes.label: AnnexI-PartII(1) — Maintain vulnerability and component records

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part II, point (1)
properties.text: Identify and document product vulnerabilities and components, including a machine-readable software bill of materials that covers at least top-level dependencies.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part II, point (2)
properties.text: Address vulnerabilities without delay by supplying security updates and, when technically feasible, keep those updates separate from feature updates.

nodes.label: AnnexI-PartII(3) — Test and review product security

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part II, point (3)
properties.text: Perform effective security testing and reviews of the product on a regular basis.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part II, point (4)
properties.text: After an update is available, publish enough information about each corrected vulnerability, affected product, impact, severity, and remediation for users to identify and address it.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part II, point (5)
properties.text: Establish and enforce a coordinated vulnerability-disclosure policy.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part II, point (6)
properties.text: Facilitate sharing information about possible product and third-party-component vulnerabilities, including by providing a vulnerability-reporting contact.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part II, point (7)
properties.text: Provide secure update-distribution mechanisms so vulnerabilities are fixed or mitigated promptly and security updates can be automatic where appropriate.

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part II, point (8)
properties.text: Distribute available security updates without delay and with clear advice on required user action, normally free of charge unless the manufacturer and a business user agree otherwise for a tailor-made product.

nodes.label: AnnexI-PartII(4)-delay — Delay disclosure only when justified

properties.source_locator: Annex I, Part II, point (4), after semicolon
properties.text: A manufacturer may postpone public information about a fixed vulnerability until users can apply the patch when a justified assessment finds publication risk greater than its security benefit.

nodes.label: SR-1 — Document the product security context

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.2.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.9
properties.text: Maintain a documented description of the security context in which the product is intended to operate.

nodes.label: SR-2 — Maintain a scoped product threat model

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.9
properties.text: Create and maintain a threat model for every product that reflects the current development scope and includes the applicable content required by this practice.

nodes.label: SR-2.a-e — Model data flows and trust structure

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.9
properties.text: Include classified information flows, trust boundaries, processes, data stores, and interacting external entities in the product threat model.

nodes.label: SR-2.f-h — Model protocols and physical interfaces

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.9
properties.text: Record implemented communication protocols, exposed physical interfaces, and board-level debug connections that could be used to attack the product.

nodes.label: SR-2.i-l — Record attack paths and security issues

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.9
properties.text: Capture potential attack vectors, threats, their severity, and identified security-related issues in the threat model.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.10
properties.text: Assign potential threats a severity using an established vulnerability-scoring method.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.10
properties.text: Document a mitigation or other disposition for every threat in the threat model.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.10
properties.text: Keep the threat model current with third-party applications, drivers, and other externally developed code linked into the product.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.10
properties.text: Review each released product's threat model at least annually and update it when emerging threats require a change even if the design is unchanged.

nodes.label: SR-2.review — Verify shared understanding of the threat model

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.10
properties.text: Have the development team review the threat model for correctness and confirm that the team understands it.

nodes.label: SR-2.issues — Route threat-model issues into defect management

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.10
properties.text: Handle issues found through threat modeling through the security-issue assessment and disposition processes.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.10
properties.text: Document product and feature security requirements, including capabilities needed for installation, operation, maintenance, and decommissioning.

nodes.label: SR-4 — Define requirement scope and target level

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.5.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.11
properties.text: For each set of security requirements, document the product's physical and logical boundaries and its target capability security level.

nodes.label: SR-5 — Review and approve security requirements

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.6.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.11
properties.text: Review, update, and approve security requirements for clarity, validity, threat-model alignment, and testability.

nodes.label: SR-5.2 — Include required disciplines in review

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §6.6.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.11
properties.text: Include implementers, independent testers, a customer advocate, and a security adviser in the security-requirements review.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §7.2.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.12
properties.text: Document each product interface, its exposure and trust boundaries, accessible assets, roles and permissions, relevant threats, safeguards, dependencies, usage, and how the design mitigates modeled threats.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §7.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.12
properties.text: Use the threat model and a risk-based approach to design multiple defensive layers.

nodes.label: SD-2.2 — Assign responsibilities to defense layers

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §7.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.12
properties.text: Assign security responsibilities to every defensive layer, apply secure design principles at each layer, and aim to reduce the attack surface exposed to subsequent layers.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §7.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.13
properties.text: For every substantial secure-design revision, identify, characterize, and track unresolved requirements, exploitable interfaces or assets, and departures from secure-design practice until closure.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §7.5.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.13
properties.text: Document secure-design practices and require their use throughout product design.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §7.5.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.13
properties.text: Regularly review and update design practices covering least privilege, proven components, simple mechanisms, secure patterns, trust boundaries, and protection or removal of development interfaces.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §7.5.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.13
properties.text: Apply attack-surface reduction as a secure-design practice.

nodes.label: SI-applicability — Limit coding controls to relevant software

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §8.2 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.15
properties.text: Apply this implementation practice's system-development requirements only to software written in a full-variability programming language.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §8.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.14
properties.text: Review implementations to find, characterize, and close security issues involving unmet requirements, coding-standard violations, and defects detectable through static analysis.

nodes.label: SI-1.sca-tool — Use an available static-analysis tool

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §8.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.14
properties.text: Perform static source analysis with a suitable tool whenever one exists for the implementation language.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §8.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.14
properties.text: Statically analyze new and modified source code, trace implementation to planned security capabilities, and assess whether threats can exploit implemented interfaces, boundaries, or assets.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §8.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.15
properties.text: Maintain and periodically update coding standards that prohibit unsafe constructs, configure analysis tools, require secure implementation techniques, validate trust-boundary inputs, and define safe error handling.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.2.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.16
properties.text: Test that product security functions satisfy their requirements and safely handle invalid input and error conditions.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.2.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.16
properties.text: Test security functionality, performance and scale, edge and stress conditions, malformed input, and trust-boundary requirements.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.16
properties.text: Test whether each mitigation for a validated threat is effective.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.16
properties.text: Plan and run tests that confirm each threat mitigation works as designed and separately attempt to defeat it.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.17
properties.text: Run tests intended to discover and characterize potential vulnerabilities in the product.

nodes.label: SVV-3.known — Use current public vulnerability information

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.17
properties.text: Base known-vulnerability testing on recent information from an established public industry source.

nodes.label: SVV-3.a — Test malformed and abusive inputs

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.17
properties.text: Use manual or automated abuse cases, fuzzing, and load or capacity tests against external interfaces and protocols where appropriate tools exist.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.17
properties.text: Identify ingress and egress paths and examine exposures such as weak access controls, open ports, and unnecessarily privileged services.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.17
properties.text: Perform black-box scans for known vulnerabilities in product hardware, hosts, and software components.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.17
properties.text: For compiled products, analyze every delivered executable and firmware image for vulnerable components or libraries, security-rule violations, and unsafe compiler settings.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.17
properties.text: Where tools are available, dynamically test for handle and memory leaks, denial-of-service conditions, and unauthenticated shared-memory access that static analysis may miss.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.5.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.18
properties.text: Perform penetration testing that attempts to exploit product weaknesses and records the resulting security defects and their characteristics.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §9.6.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.18
properties.text: Ensure the people who test the product have the required organizational independence from those who designed and implemented it.

nodes.label: DM-1 — Receive and track security reports

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.2.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.20
properties.text: Provide a process that receives security issues from internal and external reporters and tracks each one through closure.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.3.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.20
properties.text: Investigate reports promptly to determine whether they apply to the product, can be verified, and identify triggering threats.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.20
properties.text: Assess valid issues for contextual impact, severity, affected products and versions, root cause, and related issues.

nodes.label: DM-3.rca — Permit a systematic root-cause method

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.4.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.20
properties.text: A systematic method such as the referenced IEC root-cause guidance may be used when analyzing an issue's cause.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.5.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.20
properties.text: Use the impact assessment to decide how each security issue will be addressed and whether it must be reported.

nodes.label: DM-4.residual — Apply an explicit residual-risk threshold

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.5.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.20
properties.text: Set an acceptable residual-risk level and use it to choose whether to fix, compensate for, defer, disable, remove, or retain an issue, recording reasons and associated risks when resolution is deferred.

nodes.label: DM-4.all-cases — Notify affected internal and external parties

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.5.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.20
properties.text: For every disposition, inform relevant processes and product revisions and notify third parties when their included source code contains the problem.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.5.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.20
properties.text: After resolving an issue, evaluate recommendations intended to prevent similar defects from recurring.

nodes.label: DM-4.periodic — Review open issues each release cycle

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.5.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.20
properties.text: At least once per release or iteration, review unresolved security issues to confirm that their treatment remains appropriate.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.6.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.20
properties.text: Notify users promptly about reportable issues in supported products, including the issue and severity, affected versions, and the resolution.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.7.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.21
properties.text: At regular intervals, assess the security-defect process for completeness, efficiency, and successful closure of every issue handled since the preceding review.

properties.source_locator: IEC 62443-4-1:2018 §10.7.1 (clause per IEC preview ToC); text read at SDLA-312 v6.3 p.21
properties.text: Conduct the security-issue-management process review at least once each year.
